candidate: Local continuation identified by sourceSha256; no production/staging operation or backup changes.
changes: Read-request-owned promise sharing, conditional relation reads, one combined financial category catalog and exact-identity audit reuse.
Authentication skips absent collaborator/job-role reads while keeping fresh session/module/profile reads and the existing full retry boundary.
Opt-in bounded DTO cache on detail/group/point responses, after guards/query validation; scoped by user, project channel/access, financial permissions and normalized variant.

Transactional source markers: one row per PostgreSQL writer, committed full-vector hash, epoch for compaction, server/database/day identity. The 187 named source tables have statement triggers; operational jobs/sessions/telemetry excluded. No global marker write lock.
New revisions also scope intermediate derived and salary caches. Missing/failed revision checks return 503 without old responses.
Global active-pool intervals drained once across overlapping HTTP requests and aggregated by the CLI.
Job-only retention preview/apply requires explicit days, bounded batches and own audit; default scheduled retention has no JobRun policy.
Revision metadata compaction offers dry-run first, preserves active writers and advances epoch transactionally. No new scheduled job.

method.sourceParity: Eleven normalized complete surfaces in eleven states on identical real PostgreSQL rows; independent source processes; 121 equal pairs, including role/category/manual changes, official allocations/cycles, shared/manual/review/consolidated axes and changed nominal report links.
method.service: Five paired service calculations per mode/case against the original plan baseline, alternating order. Thirty equal full results. Warm database pages; imports/process boot excluded; after-session is one SELECT rather than HTTP auth.
method.http: Six sequential cohorts: control/candidate, candidate/control, then control/candidate with one periodic JobRun writer. Each has 832 measured success responses, 800 warm (100 per route/profile), eight first-process, eight warmups and sixteen after-write. Eight expected auth/module negatives separately. Final accepted total 4992 measured success responses.
method.environment: PostgreSQL 16 limited to one CPU/768 MiB; API pool eight; concurrency four; distributed group reports and point summary. No task tests/other database work during timed cohorts. API host not isolated. No proxy/TLS/browser/production load measured.
method.sourceFreeze: The 43 source/test/configuration hashes were captured before final benchmarks and checked before writing this artifact.

sparse.method: Local paired uncached service calculations on PostgreSQL with warm database pages; not HTTP latency. Timings exclude process boot and module imports. Fresh Node/Prisma processes for every cold sample. After-session performs a SELECT, not HTTP authentication. Prisma operation profiles include mapping; sqlQueries capture pg pool calls and replay SELECTs with EXPLAIN ANALYZE after the calculation. Pool call durations overlap and include queue/event-loop delays. Initialization diagnostics run in separate processes and do not warm timed samples. Result bytes are JSON sizes, not network traffic.
sparse.cpuMethod: process.cpuUsage delta around the calculation only, before EXPLAIN replay; includes Node/Prisma CPU, excludes PostgreSQL, module imports and process boot. CPU and wall time are separate observations.

limitations: Cache flag is false by default. Reuse measurements explicitly enable it; no claim of automatic production gain.
The local 95% pool result is for warmed cohorts; cold and post-write phases remain separately available. This does not accept a representative mixed production window.
A single cold HTTP sample per route/profile does not establish cold p95. Do not compose percentage reductions from separate stages.
Global source tracking conservatively invalidates on all tracked application tables. Busy real writes can reduce reuse; synthetic JobRun traffic is not a full production workload.
Markers grow with writer backend churn; bounded compaction is manual, not a new automatic policy.
Published HTTP/useful content/LCP, two-browser UI checks, worker operation and 24-hour/seven-day infrastructure series remain manual acceptance.
No JobRun cleanup period selected and no production retention applied. Backup work explicitly deferred.
